t1.text: Saved: four tiles and Playing now

n0.text:
All game data is real IGDB data from 2026-11-19: titles, years, developers, platforms, genres, summaries, covers and art.

Tweaks switches each board between dark and light.

Drawn only what games add. Backlog and Played tabs, the Played sheet, Collections and Share Links follow books and series.

n1.text:
To pick: the tiles on a phone (spec: a 2×2 grid).

A: 2×2, each tile a small fan of three covers over the name and counts.
B: 2×2, no fan on a phone: the icon, the name and the counts on two lines. The fan comes back from md.
C: one tile per row, as today, only shorter (2×2 from md only).

Playing now sits after Reading now and Watching now, the order of the tiles. A Playing row is the Reading now row: cover, title, "Developer · since 3 November", a chevron. No Progress.

n2.text:
To pick: what a result row says.

A: one muted line, "1997 · PS1", "2024 · PC, PS5, Series X|S +1".
B: the year on the line, the platforms as small outlined tags.
C: two lines: "1997 · Square Product Development Division 1", then the platforms. Search would need the developer too (one more expanded field in the same request).

n3.text:
The platforms' order (IGDB returns them unsorted: Series X|S, PS4, Switch 2, PC, PS5, XONE, Switch for The Witcher 3):
PC first, then PlayStation old to new, Xbox old to new, Nintendo old to new, then the rest by name. So The Witcher 3 reads "PC, PS4, PS5 +4", as the spec has it.

Abbreviations are IGDB's own ("XONE", "Series X|S", "famicom"). Keep them, or map a few?

n4.text:
To pick: the facts, About and the IGDB link.

A: the facts line under the title, platforms cut at three with "+4"; About is the film's: the summary cut with More, then a Genres row; "From IGDB" at About's foot is the link (where films say "From TMDB").
B: the facts line is year · developer; About gets rows as a film's Director and Cast: Platforms (all of them) and Genres. "View on IGDB" is an outline button among the actions.
C: the facts line lists every platform, wrapping; genres as tags over the summary; the link is a credit line under About: "Game details from IGDB".

n5.text:
Buttons follow books: Played (primary; "Played again" once played), Want to play (the Backlog bookmark), Start playing ("Start replaying" once played), Add to collection.

Playing card: "Playing · Since 3 November 2026", Finished (opens Played and ends Playing), Stop playing.

Stat tiles once played: Played (Once, Twice…), Your rating, First played.

n6.text:
Found while drawing: the spec's rule "the first artwork, else the first screenshot" picks a 128×128 icon for The Witcher 3 and a transparent logo for Disco Elysium (IGDB's first artworks).

IGDB tags each artwork with a type (artwork_type): key art without logo, key art with logo, artwork, concept art, logos, icons, covers, infographics.

To pick: 1 the spec as written; 2 key art first, never a logo, icon or cover, then a screenshot; 3 always a screenshot.

The pick goes into ADR-0012 and #251.

picks.text:
Picked 2026-11-19:
Saved tiles: A (2×2, a small fan over the name).
Search row: A (one line: year · platforms, "+N" past three).
The game page: A (facts cut at three, "From IGDB" is the link, a Genres row).
The banner: 2, key art first (by artwork_type), never a logo, icon or cover; then the first screenshot; then the blurred cover.
No cover: 1, typeset as a book.

n7.text:
To pick: the placeholder when IGDB has no cover.

1: typeset, as a book: the title, the developer at the foot, a thin frame.
2: one quiet icon, as a series (a gamepad on soft gold).
3: a game case: a band at the top with the first platform, the title under it.

Real games without a cover: 80's Disco Brawl (2026, PS4, Witenovastudio) and Fantasy Zone: Boss no Gyakushuu (2001, Mobile, Sonic Team). Neither has art, so the page has no banner (drawn on the Playing, no art, no cover board).
